briefing.headline: Boston + remote-US is thin today, but three of them are genuine bullseyes — and the keyword score buried two of the best.
briefing.focus: Spend the first 10 minutes on the two roles where geography, level and sponsorship all line up: CarGurus B2B Marketing Specialist (Boston, public, exactly your level) and Twilio's PLG Marketing Analyst (remote-US, and it is your analyst lane wearing a marketing title). Then fire off Stripe Capital lifecycle — your banking/fintech six years is the differentiator there, not a footnote. Everything below that is Seattle/SF relocation bets; treat Amazon and Datadog as your sponsorship insurance policy and apply broadly there, but do not let them eat the Boston roles.

ranked.why: Boston HQ, NASDAQ-listed (real sponsorship track record), B2B, and 'Specialist' is the right rung for 6 yrs without being senior — the rarest combination on today's board.
Remote-US marketing analyst on PLG funnel data — SQL + funnel metrics + attribution is literally your resume, and Twilio sponsors at scale.
Stripe Capital is lending — your six years in banking/fintech makes you a domain hire, not a generalist applicant, and it's remote-US.
Demand-gen measurement frameworks inside AWS Marketing — the exact seam between your two lanes, at the most reliable H-1B sponsor in the country.
Customer stories and case studies are a named strength of yours and most PMMs avoid this work; Datadog is public, growing, and sponsors.
An AWS PMM seat physically in Boston — worth the technical-storage stretch purely on location plus Amazon's sponsorship machinery.
'Associate' marketing ops at a public company is a clean level match, and Eloqua/HubSpot experience transfers directly; score punished it for missing Marketo, which you can learn in a week.
ABM is your first listed skill and this is a non-senior AWS ABM seat — unlike the Auto&Mfg one, which is secretly a Sr. req.
Associate-level GTM ops at Datadog explicitly recruits from mixed backgrounds; your SQL/Salesforce/funnel stack is the whole job.
Boston business analyst at a mid-size company you can actually get an onsite with — the 84 fit undersells how much geography matters for you.
B2B product marketing at Amazon Business — closest thing to a straight-across move for a B2B PMM, with sponsorship handled.
Associate title, paid LinkedIn ownership, measurable-efficiency framing — right level and your A/B testing and attribution work reads as proof.
Radar is fraud/risk — banking background is a real credential here, and the role is remote-eligible.
Remote-US at the ABM category leader; your ABM depth is the strongest possible signal, but 6sense is private and mid-size so the visa path is less certain.
GTM PMM at Stripe, listed as United States, fintech-adjacent — apply even though positioning/messaging reqs there run competitive.
Boston, public, and Salesforce/GTM systems is a credible pivot off your ops experience — but it's a product-owner job, not marketing, so expect to argue the story.
Second Boston CarGurus opening at the right level; brand is further from your B2B demand-gen core, so it's the backup to the B2B specialist req.
ABM plus partner marketing at AWS — same skill match as the NAMER ABM role, so apply to both and let the recruiter route you.
Remote-US GTM analytics is a strong lane fit, but Lattice is private, mid-size, and 'Manager' here means owning strategy for leadership.
Demand generation is the exact phrase on your resume and it's remote-US; Grafana is remote-first and open-source-flavored, so sponsorship is the open question.
Clean analyst-lane req at Amazon with no seniority qualifier — Bellevue relocation is the only real cost.
Stripe GTM planning with a US-Remote option; program-manager framing means less marketing craft and more operating cadence, but the company quality carries it.
MongoDB sponsors and NYC is commutable-adjacent, but developer lifecycle marketing is a different audience than the B2B financial buyer you know.
Sales ops analyst at a solid fintech-adjacent company and the 100 fit is fair on skills — but health-insurance ops is narrow and there's no East Coast site beyond NY.
Remote-US and Twilio sponsors, but global events management is a specialization you'd be starting from behind on versus career event marketers.
Audience and messaging is genuinely your wheelhouse and Figma is now public, but PMM reqs there draw hundreds of senior applicants.
Demand gen inside private-capital fintech is a strong content match; Carta's growth trajectory and sponsorship posture are the weak spots.
GTM strategy and planning at Gong is a good analytical fit, but no Boston or remote option and it skews toward RevOps veterans.
B2B performance marketing at specialist level and Adobe is a top-tier sponsor — the 60 fit is a scraping artifact from an empty JD, not a real signal.
ABX is ABM by another name and Workday sponsors heavily, but Pleasanton-only and a 27-day-old posting cut the odds.
Remote and freshly posted at a public IoT company, but GTM business ops is finance-flavored and the 90 ATS score oversells your match.
Anthropic is a magnet for far more experienced field marketers; worth one shot, not worth three of today's twenty minutes.
Kubernetes and GPU infrastructure PMM demands technical fluency you'd have to fake — the 97 fit is keyword noise from generic PMM vocabulary.
Associate PMM is the correct level and the low fit score is misleading, but Perplexity is SF-only and a startup visa bet.
Consumer brand campaigns for Kindle — Amazon sponsorship is the only reason this ranks; the work has nothing to do with B2B pipeline.
This is a people-manager req leading a PMM team — above your level, and the 91 score never read the word 'lead a team'.
